title: tls_stun_parse copies attacker-controlled REALM into fixed stack buffer key[0x4CE] before MESSAGE-INTEGRITY verification, causing a stack out-of-bounds write
label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:13085 char key[0x4CE] (1230 bytes)
tlse.c:13184 USERNAME attr_len is allowed up to 513
tlse.c:13254 REALM attr_len is allowed up to 763
tlse.c:13210 memcpy(ptr, realm, realm_len) starts at key+username_len+1 with no remaining-capacity check
tlse.c:13240 MESSAGE-INTEGRITY memcmp happens after the realm copy
tlse.c:14006 tls_peerconnection_iterate forwards attacker datagrams to tls_stun_parse
reason: 513+1+763 exceeds the 1230-byte key, so an unauthenticated STUN binding request overflows the stack before the HMAC check.

title: Zero-length BIT STRING in the default ASN.1 parsing branch underflows len to -1 in tls_certificate_set_sign_key, making tls_certificate_set_copy perform a SIZE_MAX memcpy heap out-of-bounds write
label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:11308 and tlse.c:11370 select the default _private_asn1_parse branch when TLS_FULL_X509 is not defined; CMakeLists.txt defines no such macro
tlse.c:11482 length==0 takes the primitive branch
tlse.c:11580-11590 a level-2 idx-3 BIT STRING calls tls_certificate_set_sign_key(cert, &buffer[pos], 0)
tlse.c:4597-4602 set_sign_key reads val[0] and decrements len to -1 when the following byte is zero
tlse.c:4546-4553 set_copy treats -1 as non-zero, calls malloc(len+1)=malloc(0), then memcpy with SIZE_MAX
tlse.c:8702 tls_parse_certificate reaches asn1_parse on peer Certificate data before verification
reason: Default-build DER parser passes a zero-length signature BIT STRING to a setter that underflows len to -1 and then performs an unbounded memcpy on glibc.

title: tls_import_context reads mac_length without a preceding bounds check, allowing a one-byte out-of-bounds read
label: UNKNOWN
evidence: tlse.c:12812 key_lengths = buffer[buf_pos++]
tlse.c:12813-12815 TLS_IMPORT_CHECK_SIZE allows key_lengths to end exactly at buf_len, leaving buf_pos == buf_len
tlse.c:12858 mac_length = buffer[buf_pos++] then reads buffer[buf_len]
examples/tlshelloworld.c:190 is the only in-repo caller and imports its own exported buffer
reason: The missing check is real and yields a 1-byte over-read on a truncated import buffer, but exploitation depends on a host importing untrusted serialized state; no leak or write is shown and the in-repo caller self-imports.

title: tls_import_context CBC branch uses uninitialized stack IV bytes
label: FP
evidence: tlse.c:12768-12769 local_iv and remote_iv are fixed 16-byte arrays
tlse.c:12798-12810 iv_len is bounded by TLS_AES_IV_LENGTH and only that many bytes are copied
tlse.c:12851 the arrays are passed to _private_tls_crypto_create
libtomcrypt.c:33364 cbc_start copies the cipher block length from the IV
reason: Only stack bytes beyond iv_len are uninitialized; the arrays are not overflowed and a caller that supplies the imported buffer already controls the session keys. No security-relevant impact is demonstrated, making this a robustness issue.

title: TLS_REEXPORTABLE import path memcpy's into a TLS_MALLOC result without a NULL check
label: UNKNOWN
evidence: tlse.c:12816 #ifdef TLS_REEXPORTABLE
tlse.c:12818-12819 TLS_MALLOC followed by memcpy with no NULL check
CMakeLists.txt and tlse.h do not define TLS_REEXPORTABLE, so the default build omits this branch
reason: The defect exists only in an opt-in TLS_REEXPORTABLE build and additionally requires allocation failure; the default frozen build does not compile the path.

title: tls_parse_verify_request reads buf[13] past the DTLS HelloVerifyRequest buffer when its body is shorter than 3 bytes
label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:7881-7886 res=11 and CHECK_SIZE(bytes_to_follow, buf_len - res) only proves L <= buf_len-11
tlse.c:7888-7889 res += 2 then len = buf[res] reads buf[13] with no remaining-length check
tlse.c:9953 case 0x03 passes the HelloVerifyRequest to tls_parse_verify_request for DTLS clients
tlse.c:9828-9830 payload_size is L+11 for DTLS
reason: A DTLS client role accepts a HelloVerifyRequest body of 0-2 bytes and reads buf[13], one to three bytes past the record's message buffer, before rejecting the record.

title: TLS 1.3 client accepts Finished without CertificateVerify, enabling certificate impersonation
label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:8613-8631 the client sets connection_status=2 after ServerHello key_share
tlse.c:9269-9329 tls_parse_finished verifies only the Finished HMAC
tlse.c:9376-9379 the TLS 1.3 client sets connection_status=0xFF after Finished
tlse.c:9985-9997 the certificate callback runs only if certificates_count is non-zero
reason: The TLS 1.3 client does not require Certificate or CertificateVerify, so an active server that controls the key share and computes Finished is accepted without proving possession of the certificate key.

title: DTLS cookie is not bound to the client source address, allowing replay to spoofed peers and amplification
label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:7775-7804 cookie is HMAC-SHA256(dtls_secret, remote_random) with no address input
tlse.c:8219 remote_random is copied from the incoming ClientHello
tlse.c:8255-8266 a fresh context builds the cookie from the same replayed random and accepts it
tlse.c:7816-7817 tls_build_verify_request uses the same process-secret cookie
reason: The DTLS cookie depends only on a process-wide secret and attacker-chosen client_random, so a cookie obtained from one source is accepted from other source addresses and fresh contexts.

title: Zero-length CBC record triggers 1-byte heap out-of-bounds read (pt[-1]) in tls_parse_message
label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:10489-10505 the CBC decryption path allocates pt=malloc(length) without rejecting length 0
libtomcrypt.c:33004-33005 cbc_decrypt returns success for len 0
tlse.c:10715 padding_byte = pt[length - 1] reads pt[-1] when length == 0
tlse.c:10494 the length>=8 guard applies only to AEAD records
reason: After a CBC cipher is installed, a zero-length record causes malloc(0) and a read of pt[-1]; reachable by a remote peer but with limited standalone impact.

title: Pre-authentication stack buffer overflow in DTLS fragmented handshake reassembly (TLSe)
label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:12524 only checks fragment_offset+fragment_length <= data_length
tlse.c:12543-12550 allocates data_length*sizeof(char*) but increments written by fragment_length without a data_length bound
tlse.c:12552 written != len keeps the fragment pending even after written exceeds len
tlse.c:9802 local_buffer is DTLS_MAX_FRAGMENT_SIZE+12 bytes on the stack
tlse.c:9832 and tlse.c:9847 use written as the memcpy length into local_buffer
reason: Overlapping DTLS fragments accumulate written far beyond data_length; a later non-fragmented record copies written bytes into the fixed stack buffer, overflowing it pre-authentication.

title: Chain validation ignores basicConstraints and keyUsage: a non-CA certificate can issue certificates that TLSe reports as verified
label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:11076-11184 signature verification never inspects basicConstraints or keyUsage
tlse.c:11212-11238 tls_certificate_chain_is_valid checks dates and signatures only
tlse.c:11250-11305 tls_certificate_chain_is_valid_root checks issuer name, dates, and signature only
reason: A certificate marked CA:FALSE, or whose keyUsage omits keyCertSign, is accepted as an issuer whenever its signature verifies to a loaded trust anchor.

title: Out-of-bounds write in tls_certificate_to_string(): negative size passed to snprintf once the rendered peer certificate exceeds the caller's buffer
label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:4612-4623 res accumulates snprintf return values and the next call uses len - res
tlse.c:4716-4719 and tlse.c:4750-4751 repeat the same pattern for key and signature output
no check requires res < len before buffer + res and len - res are used
reason: Once the rendered certificate exceeds the caller's len, len-res becomes negative and is converted to size_t, so snprintf writes past the caller's buffer with attacker-influenced certificate fields.

title: DTLS short handshake record causes out-of-bounds read of the fragment header in tls_consume_stream
label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:12498 length is the record length field plus the 13-byte DTLS header
tlse.c:12508 the only guard is length > 13
tlse.c:12512-12516 twelve fragment-header bytes are read from buffer+13 without checking that the record carries them
reason: A DTLS handshake record with 1-11 payload bytes passes length > 13 and reads up to 11 bytes past the record/allocation while filling fragment bookkeeping fields.

title: Stale public-key/signature length after the key is cleared leads to a NULL pointer dereference in tls_certificate_to_string()
label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:4581-4588 tls_certificate_set_key frees the old key through set_copy but updates pk_len only when the new pointer is non-NULL
tlse.c:4546-4557 tls_certificate_set_copy sets *member=NULL when len is zero
tlse.c:11580-11593 the parser can invoke set_key again with a zero-length BIT STRING at the pk_id path
tlse.c:4718-4719 tls_certificate_to_string iterates pk_len and dereferences cert->pk
reason: A certificate that sets the key twice, the second time empty, leaves pk NULL with a stale non-zero pk_len; rendering the certificate then dereferences NULL.

title: Client-certificate authentication is not enforced: handshake completes without a client certificate and tls_client_verified() returns true for an untrusted self-signed certificate
label: UNKNOWN

tlse.c:9995-9996 the verification callback runs only when certificates_count is non-zero
tlse.c:10085-10108 Finished completes the handshake even when no client certificate was processed
tlse.c:12980-12984 tls_client_verified reports only the client_verified flag
reason: The source permits empty client certificates and delegates trust validation to the optional application callback; whether this bypasses authentication depends on application gating and callback installation, which cannot be resolved from the snapshot.

title: No DTLS anti-replay window: captured application-data records are re-delivered to the application indefinitely
label: TP
evidence: tlse.c:10787-10791 remote_sequence_number is overwritten from each received DTLS record
tlse.c:10554-10557 AEAD nonce and AAD are derived from the record's own epoch/sequence
no replay window or highest-sequence comparison exists in the DTLS receive path
reason: The DTLS record layer keeps no anti-replay state, so a captured record remains cryptographically valid and is delivered to the application again arbitrarily late.
